ap_computer_science_a-m04.stem: Which of the following is the weakest precondition (the least restrictive condition) that guarantees the method will not throw an exception?

options.text: s has at least two characters.
options.why: The call fails when this condition is false: substring is asked for characters that are not there, which throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. When it is true the method works.

options.text: Every String argument contains only letters.
options.why: The characters are never examined, only the positions, so the kind of character does not matter.

options.text: The String arguments are different from each other.
options.why: The method works when the arguments are equal, so no such condition is needed.

options.text: Every String argument contains at least ten characters.
options.why: Two characters (or one per argument) are enough; requiring ten is much more than the method needs.

blueprint.subject: ap_computer_science_a
blueprint.concept: a precondition states what must hold on entry for the method to work
student_thinking: read the code and decide which statement about it is true
compare the result with each option and rule out the named misconceptions

key_conditions.condition: each claim was checked by compiling or running the code with the JDK

misconceptions.description: The characters are never examined, only the positions, so the kind of character does not matter.
The method works when the arguments are equal, so no such condition is needed.
Two characters (or one per argument) are enough; requiring ten is much more than the method needs.

verification.independent_path: java runs on a failing and a working call

blueprint.judgment_demand: separate the true statement from the named misconceptions

ap_computer_science_a-m05.stem: Which of the following best describes the postcondition of the method steps (what is true about the returned value when the method finishes)?

options.text: It returns how many times 4 can be subtracted from n before the remaining value is less than 4; this is the quotient n / 4.
options.why: The loop subtracts 4 until fewer than 4 remain and counts the subtractions, which equals n / 4 using integer division.

options.text: It returns the remainder when n is divided by 4.
options.why: The loop counts subtractions in c; the remainder is the final value of n, which is not returned.
The loop keeps subtracting while at least 4 remain, and the method returns the count rather than a value related to n minus 4.

options.text: It returns the number of digits in n written in base 4.
options.why: The loop does not divide repeatedly; it subtracts once per pass, which is not the digit count.
